messages:
Ellen: Noticed a subtle p95 regression for tiny requests after the kernel-selector roll last night on pool-omega. Dash: https://dash.redwood/host/pool-omega/p95 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Raj: saw the alert. Any change in the batching histogram or kvcache metrics?
Ellen: running_batch median shifted 4 -> 1.8 on impacted hosts. KV remote-fallback rate +2.7%. grpc smallwrite syscall rate +18%.
Marta: That pattern smells like the selector picked a high-throughput kernel for long sequences that has worse per-request startup cost for short sequences. Lower throughput per-core -> lower in-flight concurrency -> more 1-item batches -> kvcache hot-shard contention -> remote fetches -> additional smallwrites. Self-reinforcing loop.
Tom: Can you paste a representative trace? want parse/tokenize/kernel/net split.
Ellen: pasted (trimmed):
```
2025-06-02T22:14:01.201 parse_request 0.9ms
2025-06-02T22:14:01.203 tokenize      3.3ms (unicode-normalize pass)
2025-06-02T22:14:01.207 kvcache_lookup 0.5ms (miss -> remote fetch 4.9ms)
2025-06-02T22:14:01.213 kernel_exec   21.6ms (chosen: fused_vector)
2025-06-02T22:14:01.238 grpc_writev   5.1ms (3 small frames)
```
Raj: tokenization cost is now a bigger fraction. But kernel_exec jump + remote fetch kills tail.
Marta: Short-term mitigation: soft-rollback selector on canary + add a gating rule: if observed running_batch_p90 < 3 OR recent_kv_remote_rate > 1% prefer the lightweight kernel. Also emit kernel_variant label per-host and a `running_batch_size` histogram metric.
Ellen: Agreed. infra-bot can we do a soft-rollback on pool-omega canary?
infra-bot: Received. Initiating soft-rollback of selector config on pool-omega canary. ETA ~90s.
deploy-bot: Soft-rollback started at 22:17:12 UTC.
Tom: For longer term: selector scoring should include an end-to-end host_cost estimate. Today it uses kernel token throughput only. New score = kernel_exec_ms_est + median_tokenize_ms_est + expected_network_syscall_cost. If host_preproc dominates for shape S, prefer the lighter kernel even if pure kernel throughput would prefer heavy kernel.
Marta: Also two experiments to run: 1) co-located tokenization sidecar for ultra-short requests (removes tokenize CPU from host, adds RPC overhead), 2) tune gRPC coalescing/writev thresholds on host to reduce small syscall count. Add both to the replay matrix.
Raj: I'll queue a replay: 3k requests, 32 tokens, model=omega-smallshape, compare kernels + sidecar + writev-coalesce.
Ellen: Please attach replay traces to the RFC. Also add alert rules: running_batch_p50 drop >1.5 OR kvcache_remote_rate increase >1% to abort selector rollout earlier.
infra-bot: Soft-rollback complete at 22:18:45 UTC. Canary p95 trending back toward baseline.
Marta: For telemetry, prefer labels on metrics: `kernel_variant`, `host_pool`, `running_batch_p50`, `kvcache_remote_rate`, `grpc_smallwrite_count`. Derived metric: `host_kernel_end2end_est_ms` = kernel_exec_ms + median_tokenize_ms + median_writev_syscall_ms. Emit per-host.
Tom: Nice. In the RFC include: profiling flamegraphs (host-side stages), perf counters for syscall counts, and replay artifacts. Also add a small preflight micro-benchmark (2k tiny requests) that runs as part of selector config rollouts and fails the rollout when the derived metric worsens by >3% on canary.
Raj: Replay queued: https://replay.redwood/jobs/1772468101-3k-32t. ETA ~6m. Will post trimmed traces.
Ellen: Closing the immediate alert. Follow-ups: RFC for selector score change + gating rule + telemetry + CI replay. Thanks all :thumbsup:
